sentences.text:
Respondents  CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAJESH SHANKAR  -----
For the Petitioners : Mr. Rajiv Kumar, Advocate Mr. Niraj Kr Singh, Advocate For the Respondents :
Mr. Manoj Kumar, GA-III -----
I.A. No. 10232 of 2023 17/10.06.2024 The present interlocutory application has been filed on behalf of the petitioners seeking amendment in the relief as well as pleadings made in the writ petition in view of supplementary counter affidavit filed on behalf of the respondents.
2. Mr. Rajiv Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioners, does not press the present interlocutory application.
3. I.A. No. 10232 of 2023 is accordingly dismissed as not pressed.

4. In course of argument, learned counsel for the petitioners, refers to order dated 11.01.2024 (particularly paragraph no. 3 of the same), which reads as under:
"Admittedly, a Police Station has been constructed on the part of the land which belongs to the petitioner.
The area is five decimals over which the construction is made.
Admittedly, the petitioner is the title holder of the entire land including the portion over which the Police Station has been constructed, which has also been declared by a competent Civil Court.

Therefore, now the only issue which remains to be decided is whether the respondents be directed to demolish the Police Station and hand over vacant possession of the land to the petitioner or to pay compensation as per the provision of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Ajay Kumar Singh & Anr vs The State Of Jharkhand Through The ... on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197478334/
1 Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 for the five decimals of land, over which the Police Station is constructed.
So far as vacant portion is concerned, which has been bounded by the boundary wall by the respondents will be demarcated from the five decimals of land, over which the Police Station has been constructed.

entities.text: Ajay Kumar Singh & Anr vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The respondents are injuncted from entering into the vacant portion i.e. the area beyond the constructed Police Station.

Whether the respondents are ready to pay compensation or they are ready to demolish the Police Station, will be informed to this Court on the next date.
List this case after two weeks."
5.

According to learned counsel for the petitioners, it would be clear from the judgment dated 17.06.2009 passed in Title Appeal No. 15/2006 that the petitioners had the rightful ownership over 5 acres of Plot No. 78/Revisional Survey Plot No. 160, Khata No. 206/Revisional Survey Khata No.
285 of Village- Sarki, P.S.-Manjhiaon, District-Garhwa.
The respondent authorities had constructed outpost in 5 decimals of the said land and subsequently, a police station was also constructed over the additional 5 decimals land.

Since the petitioners had been given possession of 25 decimals out of 5 acres of the said land during the execution process, they deserved to be returned the rest 4.75 acres of land by the respondent authorities.

6. Mr. Manoj Kumar, learned GA-III appearing on behalf of the respondents, refers to paragraph no.
9 of the counter affidavit dated 12.09.2023 filed on behalf of the respondent nos. 2 and 3, which reads as under:
"9. That it is further submitted and stated on behalf of the answering respondents that a record has been opened on the basis of modified Acquisition proposal presented by the respondent No. 3 but in the meantime, it is revealed from the report submitted by the Circle Officer, Kandi vide letter no. 62 dated 04.04.2022 that final publication of record of right of the Revisional Survey has already been made u/s 83(2) of the CNT Act, in which the new Khata number of the subject land has been changed as R.S. Khata No. 285 appertaining to R.S. Plot No. 160 (wrongly mentioned as Plot No. 107), area 3.03 acre and the same is recorded as "Anabad Jharkhand Sarkar" and in the remark column mentioned as illegal possession since 1979 of Dukhabhanjan Shukla.
The said R.S. Khatiyan was published on 23.11.2007.

Due to such conflict the preliminary notification u/s 11(1) of Act No. 30/2013 has not been Noticed/Published."
7.
It is thus submitted by learned GA-III that R.S. Plot No. 160, R.S. Khata No. 285, measuring an area of 3.03 acres is a government land.

8. Learned counsel for the State shall address the Court on the issue as to whether the remaining part of the land appertaining to old Plot No. 78, New Plot No. 160, old Khata No. 206, New Khata Ajay Kumar Singh & Anr vs The State Of Jharkhand Through The ... on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197478334/
2 No. 285, Mouza-Sarki over which the petitioners claim their raiyati land right is justified.
